A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LT3SD and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite appendix reorganization and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D-FRONT generation and completion experiments, quantitative comparisons, representation ablations, novelty analyses, and supplementary timing results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds XCube comparisons, another resolution ablation, and an outdoor city generation result.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated reconstruction objective: Equation (3) changes from a loss summed across resolution levels to a per-level squared reconstruction loss. The latent-tree architecture, diffusion conditioning, and patch-wise generation procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1's empirical coverage concerns indoor 3D-FRONT scenes. v2 adds training on the cited 'Full gameready city buildings' asset and outdoor city generation in Appendix A.4 and Figure 9, extending the represented domain beyond indoor houses.

E2.justification: XCube moves from related-work discussion to an evaluated comparator in Table 1, Figure 4, and supplementary Figure 10. This adds a directly relevant sparse-voxel hierarchy competitor to the earlier PVD, NFD, and BlockFusion comparison.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce an 8.8-to-2.2 cm single-level control, outdoor outputs of resolution 1536×1536×512, and an adapted two-level XCube setup. Existing splits, voxel resolution, training budgets, and metrics are retained. Appendix B.1's newly specified evaluation patch sizes do not establish a revision to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a single-level 8.8-to-2.2 cm ablation alongside the retained single-level and multilevel configurations, testing the hierarchy benefit at another latent resolution. Existing novelty retrieval, representation comparisons, intermediate visualizations, and sequential-versus-parallel timing ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or formal significance tests. Both use point estimates and qualitative examples.

E6.justification: New XCube results materially qualify the comparative ranking: v2 Table 1 reports MMD-CD/EMD of 3.35/26.14 for XCube versus 3.51/27.30 for full LT3SD, although LT3SD retains better FID, 13.39 versus 55.35. The new single-level ablation reports FID 50.07, and Figure 9 adds outdoor results. Previously reported numerical entries are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (3) removes the cross-resolution summation and its accompanying description, revising the formal reconstruction-loss definition. Other mathematical definitions, diffusion equations, inference equations, and supplementary metric formulas are retained; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the latent-tree and patch-wise diffusion contributions, arbitrary-sized scene generation and completion claims, and the stated 70% FID improvement. The added experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes XCube's weaker local detail to whole-scene generation, explains storage savings through fewer latent channels, and motivates the half-patch overlap through context and seam reduction. Appendix A adds discussion of outdoor applicability and potential uses in games, robotic training, and film production.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies 5.6×5.6×2.8 m FID patches and subdivision into 2.8 m cubes for point metrics. Appendix B.2 documents XCube grid sizes, GPU-memory constraints, and use of its pretrained Objaverse refinement network. The outdoor asset source is also supplied; existing LT3SD implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to 3DTopia-XL, LN3Diff, TRELLIS, and the city asset. Related work incorporates TRELLIS and expands the explanation of outdoor methods' geometry limitations; Appendix A.2 adds a contrast with the already cited DiffuScene's single-room object-layout focus.

P1.justification: Changes comprise targeted prose edits, standardized units, and a new acknowledgement. The appendix exchanges the novelty and infinite-scene subsection order and organizes evaluation into metrics, baselines, and additional comparisons. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and revised resolution and scale labels. Figure 4 and the supplementary comparison gain an XCube column. A new outdoor Figure 9 is inserted; the earlier supplementary comparison and infinite-scene figures become Figures 10 and 11, with associated layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The XCube comparison and additional resolution control address gaps in v1's evaluation, while Appendix B improves reproducibility. These provide a limited net gain. Outdoor support remains qualitative, and Table 1's retained claim of superiority on all metrics is not reconciled with XCube's better MMD results.
